label: Pali yak

about.text: The Pali yak is one of the milked yak populations of China, named in a study of Chinese yak milk. In that study its milk had about 5.7 percent protein, 6.0 percent fat and 16.3 percent milk solids.

sources.text: Opened with WebFetch. Table 1, 'Composition of substances in different types of yak milk (%)', gives Pali (China): milk solids 16.3, fat 6.0, protein 5.7, lactose 3.8, ash not available. The table cites refs 7, 16 and 17 for the whole table; the paper gives no sample size or year for this population. The Tibet location is not in this paper; see origin.

Found in WebSearch text only (page not opened): the DAGRIS country breed pages describe Pali yak in Tibet. A WebSearch summary of a 1997-1998 Tibetan survey names Pali as one of three breeds in Tibet, and of a 2020 study places Pali in Yadong county. No formation date was found.
Table 1 of the paper, read through WebFetch: fat 6.0, protein 5.7, lactose 3.8, milk solids 16.3 (all %). Single figures, so min equals max.
The paper reports the milk composition of this population, so it is treated as a milked dairy population. No other use was researched.

gaps: Not found: a population count for this breed (the only counts found were for all Tibetan yak), any formation date, the herdbook or DAD-IS entry, the yield per lactation, the risk status, and sample size or year for the composition figures. The paper's Table 1 cites refs 7, 16 and 17 for all rows, not for this row alone. The source's claim that Pali has the highest protein of those listed is not used: Tianzhu White's protein range runs to 6.5 in the same table. Aka names, domestication and facts were not researched.
